Mutual expectations · The last page

The relationship I want

The first three pages are about how not to lose: how to check a statistic, how to spot being tricked out of money, how to set thresholds. This page is the reverse — once all those defences hold, what is it that I actually want? It is not a list of demands to make of someone else; it is about writing the standard down first, then choosing people by it, and holding myself to it too.

Money and giving Feelings and respect Growing as a person Bottom lines
01

On money and giving

On money there is only one standard: neither of us lives off the other.

Independence and going Dutch

I hope we can both be financially independent and not rely on each other for basic living costs. On dates we can take turns paying or split the bill, rather than one person covering everything.

Refusing hidden extraction

I do not want our relationship built on material exchange. For example, my love should not be questioned because I do not buy a designer bag or a phone, and neither of us should use coldness or arguments to force the other to give in.

Be careful about borrowing money

Soon after meeting, I would never ask the other person for a loan or a red envelope. If help really is needed, I would say so honestly and repay promptly, rather than using it to test or wear down the relationship.

02

On feelings and respect

A relationship should see daylight; warmth should be everyday.

An open relationship

Once we are together, I would like to be introduced to friends and family and to have the relationship public in your social circle, rather than being made invisible.

Equal emotional investment

I hope you will share your life and your past so I can know the real you. And your warmth should not appear only when a gift arrives — it should be everyday care and company.

Refusing emotional blackmail

Love is respect, not control. No pressuring with "if you loved me you would", no cold war over small things — problems get solved by talking.

03

On growing as a person

Only two whole people can truly attract each other.

Growing together

I hope we both focus on growing ourselves instead of relying on the other to fill an inner gap. Real love is two independent souls drawn to each other, not two love-starved people tangled together.

Inner strength and confidence

I hope you have steady emotions and self-confidence, and that outside opinions do not shake your sense of worth. Only then can you see what a relationship really is and not be blinded by empty sweet talk.

04

Bottom lines

These three leave no room for interpretation.

Honesty and transparency

From the start I will tell you my real name and living situation, and hide nothing important.

Refusing deception

If I find fraud, gambling or similar behaviour, I will cut losses immediately and not hesitate over sunk costs.

Legal awareness

For large transfers I note the purpose, to protect both sides' interests — but that should be a last line of defence, not the normal way of being together.

One last thing

Real love makes you a better version of yourself, not servile, anxious or poor. If someone can only be kept with your money,then what she loves is not you but your money.

May we all meet the person who did not come for the money, but stayed for love.
